beats.text: Straight men orgasm ninety-five percent of the time. Guess women.
In bed, there's a gap nobody talks about.
A survey of over fifty thousand American adults asked how often they orgasm during sex.
Straight men: ninety-five percent. Straight women: sixty-five. But one group closes the gap.
So it's not just biology. Women who orgasmed more often got more oral sex, longer sessions, and asked for what they wanted.
The gap is real. And it can be closed. Start by talking.

sources: Frederick, St. John, Garcia & Lloyd (2018, online 2017). Differences in orgasm frequency among gay, lesbian, bisexual, and heterosexual men and women in a U.S. national sample. Archives of Sexual Behavior 47(1). N = 52,588. Usually-always orgasm: heterosexual men 95%, gay men 89%, bisexual men 88%, lesbian women 86%, bisexual women 66%, heterosexual women 65%. Women who orgasmed more: received more oral sex, longer duration of last sex, asked for what they want, more relationship satisfaction. Via Chapman University Digital Commons abstract.
